name: CI

# The quality spine, enforced in CI on every push + PR. This runs the FULL set:
# everything the fast pre-push runs PLUS the heavy typed lint and knip (which are
# kept OUT of pre-push so local pushes stay snappy). A push/PR that drops below the
# bar fails here, not just on a developer's machine.
#
# EDIT: rename this file to .github/workflows/ci.yml in your repo. Adjust the Node
# version and, if your @-scoped deps live in a sibling repo, add a checkout step
# for it (see the commented block).

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22' # EDIT: match your repo's Node version
          cache: npm

      # EDIT: if @-scoped deps are `file:` links to a sibling monorepo, check it out
      # and build it here before `npm ci` (mirror your local layout).

      - name: Install deps
        run: npm ci

      - name: Format check (prettier)
        run: npm run format:check

      - name: Lint (TYPED - the AI-dead-code net; slow, CI-only)
        run: npm run lint

      - name: Knip (module-level dead code; CI-only)
        run: npm run knip

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      - name: Tests + coverage gate (>=85% all dimensions)
        run: npm run coverage:check

      - name: Dependency-cruiser (no circular imports / boundary breaks)
        run: npm run depcruise

      - name: jscpd DRY gate (duplication under threshold)
        run: npm run jscpd

      - name: Production build
        run: npm run build

name: CI

# The quality spine for a React Native repo, enforced in CI on every push + PR.
# Runs the FULL set: everything the fast pre-push runs PLUS the heavy typed lint
# and knip (kept out of pre-push for speed). A push/PR below the bar fails here.
#
# EDIT: rename to .github/workflows/ci.yml. The Metro bundle step is the RN
# stand-in for a production build (bundler/resolver errors tsc+jest miss).

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22' # EDIT: match your repo's Node version
          cache: npm

      - name: Install deps
        run: npm ci

      - name: Format check (prettier)
        run: npm run format:check

      - name: Lint (TYPED - the AI-dead-code net; slow, CI-only)
        run: npm run lint

      - name: Knip (module-level dead code; CI-only)
        run: npm run knip

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      - name: Tests + coverage gate (>=85% all dimensions)
        run: npm run coverage:check

      - name: Dependency-cruiser (no circular imports / boundary breaks)
        run: npm run depcruise

      - name: jscpd DRY gate (duplication under threshold)
        run: npm run jscpd

      - name: Metro bundle (catches resolver/bundle errors)
        run: npx react-native bundle --platform android --dev true --entry-file index.js --bundle-output /tmp/ci.bundle --reset-cache

# code-check SETUP: the quality-as-code spine

Run this in a JavaScript or TypeScript repo to install the whole quality spine in one shot: the
libraries, plugins, configs, gates, the pre-push hook, and the CI workflow. Every
repo that runs it inherits the same standard, so quality is code, not memory.

The script and the files that are code (`bootstrap.sh`, `.dependency-cruiser.js`, `.prettierrc`,
`githooks/pre-push`) are stored here as `<file>.md`, with the code in a `~~~~~` fence. Write them out first with
the "Bundled files" command in `../SKILL.md`, which copies the skill to `$OUT`, then:

```bash
bash "$OUT/setup/bootstrap.sh"          # from the target repo root
bash "$OUT/setup/bootstrap.sh" /path    # or pass the repo path
```

`<skill-folder>` is wherever your agent installed this skill, for example
`.claude/skills/code-check`. Set `HYGIENE_SKIP_INSTALL=1` to place the
configs without running `npm install`.

`bootstrap.sh` is idempotent and non-destructive. Re-run it any time; it skips what
is already in place and never silently clobbers an edited config (it backs the old
one up to `<file>.hygiene.bak` first).

## What gets installed

| Artifact | Gate it powers |
| --- | --- |
| `.prettierrc` | Formatting baseline (web: 120 cols, RN: 80 cols). |
| `.eslintrc.json` | Typed lint + the AI-dead-code rules, with a plugin set for the stack. |
| `.dependency-cruiser.js` | No eager-value circular imports (the load-bearing rule) + architecture boundaries. |
| `.jscpd.json` | DRY copy/paste detector, baseline-then-ratchet threshold. |
| `.c8rc.json` | `>=85%` coverage on the pure-logic layer; I/O glue excluded and documented. |
| `knip.json` | Module-level dead code (unused files/exports/deps). |
| `.githooks/pre-push` | Fast local gate. Wired via `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`. |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | Full gate, including the heavy typed lint + knip. |
| `tsconfig.json` (merged) | `allowUnreachableCode:false`, `noUnusedLocals:true`, `noUnusedParameters:true`. |
| `package.json` scripts | `format`, `format:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `depcruise`, `jscpd`, `knip`, `coverage`, `coverage:check`, `hooks:install`, and `build` if absent. |

### The three layers of dead-code detection

They are complementary, not redundant:

1. `@typescript-eslint/no-unnecessary-condition` and friends find dead BRANCHES
   inside a file (the always-true guard, the `?.` on a non-nullable) - the classic
   AI-generated dead branch.
2. `dependency-cruiser` finds cycles and boundary breaks between files.
3. `knip` finds whole unused files, exports, and dependencies.

## How stack detection works

`bootstrap.sh` sniffs `package.json` deps plus marker config files, in priority
order:

1. **React Native** - `metro.config.js` present, or a `react-native` dependency.
   Uses the RN baseline (airbnb + fp + react-native plugins, 80-col prettier, Metro
   bundle as the build gate).
2. **Web (Next.js / React)** - `next.config.*` present, or a `next` or `react`
   dependency. Uses the web baseline (eslint:recommended + sonarjs + security +
   github plugins, 120-col prettier, `next build` as the build gate).
3. **Plain TS library** - none of the above, just `typescript`. Reuses the web
   templates (the Next.js-specific globs simply match nothing) with `tsc --noEmit`
   as the build gate.

## The pre-push vs CI split (deliberate)

Two gates run different subsets, on purpose:

- **Pre-push (fast, local):** format check, typecheck, coverage, dependency-cruiser,
  jscpd, build. Kept snappy so pushing is not painful.
- **CI (full, every push + PR):** everything pre-push runs PLUS the **heavy typed
  eslint** (`parserOptions.project` makes it slow) and **knip**. CI is the backstop
  that always runs the full set.

If you want the typed lint locally too, add `npm run lint` to `.githooks/pre-push`
and accept the slower push. The contract is: CI always runs everything.

## The ratchet philosophy (baseline-then-ratchet)

A repo with an existing backlog will not pass every gate on day one, and that is
expected. You baseline at the current reality, then ratchet the bar UP as you burn
the backlog down. Never loosen a gate to excuse a new problem.

- **`no-unnecessary-condition`:** if it floods a repo with a real backlog, set it to
  `"warn"` in `.eslintrc.json`, drive the count to zero, then flip it back to
  `"error"`. A clean repo starts at `"error"`.
- **`.jscpd.json` threshold:** run `npm run jscpd` once, read the reported
  duplication percentage, set `threshold` JUST ABOVE it (not zero - that fails
  immediately on any existing code), then ratchet it DOWN as you extract clones.
- **`.c8rc.json`:** the `>=85%` bar applies to the pure-logic layer. Exclude your
  genuine I/O glue so the bar is reachable (see the exclusion rule below), never
  exclude branching logic to game the number.

## Honest per-repo tuning you still have to do

The bootstrap gets you a working spine, but three things are genuinely repo-specific
and cannot be auto-detected:

1. **`.dependency-cruiser.js` boundary globs.** The `pure-lib-no-io`, `lib-no-app`,
   and `no-route-to-route` rules assume `src/lib` (pure logic + adapters) and
   `src/app` (routes). Every glob marked `# EDIT:` needs your real directory layout.
   The `no-circular` rule works with no edits - it is the one that matters most.
2. **`knip.json` ignore entries for dynamic entry points.** knip cannot see a module
   reached ONLY through a dynamic `import()`, a string-keyed registry, or a
   navigation route table - it will flag it as unused. The workflow is **annotate,
   do not delete:** when knip flags something that IS reached dynamically, add it to
   `ignore` (or tag the export with a `// knip-ignore` comment). Deleting a real
   dynamic entry point is how knip breaks a build. This is manual and ongoing.
3. **`.c8rc.json` I/O-glue exclusion list.** Replace the example files with your real
   thin adapters. The rule for excluding a file: it must be a thin I/O adapter whose
   pure decision half already lives in a tested sibling module (a `*-policy` /
   `*-shape` / `*-plan` / `*-rules` module). If a file has branching logic and no
   pure sibling, do not exclude it - extract the pure half and test it.

Also: the coverage scripts wrap `npm test`, so define your test runner (`node --test`,
`jest`, or `vitest run`) as the `test` script. The bootstrap warns if it is missing.

## Customizing

- **eslint 9 flat config:** the templates use the legacy `.eslintrc.json` so the full
  plugin set composes cleanly. If your repo is flat-config-only, port the same
  `extends` / `plugins` / `rules` into `eslint.config.js` - the RULES are the
  contract, not the file format.
- **Different Node version in CI:** edit `node-version` in `github-workflows-ci.yml`.
- **Sibling monorepo deps:** if your `@`-scoped deps are `file:` links to a sibling
  repo, add a checkout + build step in the CI workflow before `npm ci` (there is a
  commented placeholder for it).

## Provenance

Generalized from the gate-green configs of a production web app (`.dependency-cruiser.js`,
`.jscpd.json`, `.c8rc.json`, `.githooks/pre-push`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`,
`package.json` scripts) and two public baselines: `wednesday-solutions/react-template`
(web) and `wednesday-solutions/react-native-template` (React Native).

# Pick the right AI models for your app

![How pick-the-best-ai-model works](../../../assets/skills/pick-the-best-ai-model.png)

Your agent reads which models your app uses today, researches what else could ship for each kind of model and each device, and hands you a sourced table of Add, Replace, Keep, Later and Remove calls. Once you approve, it writes the picks into your app's model list.

**Use it when**

- New models came out and you want to know if any beat what you ship.
- You are choosing models for a new feature such as transcription, voice or image generation.
- You need different picks for small and large devices.

**Try it:** "Which transcription and chat models should our app ship for phones with 8 GB and desktops with 16 GB?"

# Get a one-page decision report you can approve from the first screen

![How help-me-decide works](../../../assets/skills/help-me-decide.png)

Your agent writes one page with the answer first, every claim linked to a source, at least three options scored on points you set, and separate reviewers checking the facts and the reasoning before you see it.

**Use it when**

- You have to pick between options and want the case laid out fairly.
- Someone asks you for a decision paper or board paper.
- You want a recommendation you can trust, not a confident guess.

**Try it:** "Help me decide whether to hire a growth lead, use an agency, or keep doing it ourselves. Write it up so I can decide."

# Deploy on any day without holding your breath

Before a production deploy, your agent checks CI, env vars, migrations and the rollback plan. After it, it checks health, the flows that make you money, errors and latency, and tells you to roll back the moment the numbers say so.

Use it when:
- You're about to deploy to production.
- You just deployed and want to know it's really fine.
- Last time you deployed, something broke and nobody noticed for an hour.

Try it: "/deploy-without-fear we're shipping v2.3 to prod"

# Get your articles found and quoted by search and AI answers

![How get-cited-by-ai works](../../../assets/skills/get-cited-by-ai.png)

Your agent plans and writes articles that answer the question a reader would actually type, with the answer up top, facts checked against the source, and one clear next step. The same structure helps Google and AI answer engines understand and quote the page.

Use it when:
- You want a list of article titles people would search for.
- You're writing or revising a how-to, a "best X" list or a README meant to bring in users.
- You want to know which of your existing articles work and why, without guessing.

Try it: "/get-cited-by-ai Plan ten article titles for our app from the last three releases."

# Your AI stops breaking things that already worked

You fix one bug and two old features break. Every change gets tested by tapping through your app like a real user, with no mocks hiding the breakage.

![How your ai stops breaking things that already worked works](../assets/sets/testing-how-it-works.png)

| Skill | What you get |
| --- | --- |
| [**test-like-a-user**](skills/test-like-a-user) | Tests that open the real screen, tap the real button and check what you'd see. No mocks of your own code. |
| [**bug-trap**](skills/bug-trap) | Every bug gets a test that fails first, so it can't sneak back in. |
| [**dont-break-it**](skills/dont-break-it) | Your AI changes, checks and saves code so nothing half-done ships. |
| [**fix-it-for-real**](skills/fix-it-for-real) | It fixes the cause, not the symptom, and reuses what someone already solved. |
| [**click-everything**](skills/click-everything) | It clicks through every page of your web app and fixes what breaks. |

## Install just this set

```bash
npx skills add off-grid-ai/skills --skill test-like-a-user bug-trap dont-break-it fix-it-for-real click-everything
```

Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add off-grid-ai/skills` then `/plugin install off-grid-testing@off-grid-ai`.
Codex: `codex plugin marketplace add off-grid-ai/skills` then `codex plugin add off-grid-testing@off-grid-ai`.

Some of these skills call skills in other sets. To get everything working together, install every set (see the main README).

[All skills](../README.md)

# Tests that catch real bugs

![How bug-trap works](../../../assets/skills/bug-trap.png)

A short checklist your agent follows every time it touches a test. You get tests that break when behaviour breaks, not when a button moves, and failures that get fixed at the cause.

Use it when:
- Your agent is about to write, change or fix a test.
- Tests keep breaking after harmless UI changes.
- Someone wants to "just raise the timeout" on a failing test.

Try it: "Add tests for the export feature, following bug-trap."

# Playtest every scene of your game, with pictures

![How playtest works](../../../assets/skills/playtest.png)

Your agent builds a checklist of every screen and scene, renders and checks each one, and reports pass or fail with a screenshot. It also scores how fun a real session is against the last run.

Use it when:
- You want to know what is broken across the whole game, not one scene.
- You are about to cut a build or a release.
- You changed a shared system and want to see what it touched.

Try it: "Playtest every scene and tell me what's broken, with screenshots."

# Change code in small, safe, checked commits

![How dont-break-it works](../../../assets/skills/dont-break-it.png)

Your agent follows the project's own rules, keeps changes additive, checks once in the background, and commits one change at a time with hooks on.

**Use it when**

- Your agent is about to edit code, run checks or commit.
- You want small commits that are easy to review and revert.
- You want no skipped hooks and no waiting on long builds.

**Try it:** "Fix the date bug in the reports page and commit it the safe way."

# Tests for code that never had any

Point your agent at a flow in old code. It works out what the code does today, writes end-to-end tests in tiers from sure to likely, runs every one and fixes them until they pass. What it can't test becomes a checklist, and any bug it finds comes first.

Use it when:
- You need to refactor code with no tests.
- You've inherited a project and don't trust it yet.
- Your most important flow has no tests at all.

Try it: "/tests-for-old-code the signup and email verification flow"

# Fix the real problem, not the symptom

![How fix-it-for-real works](../../../assets/skills/fix-it-for-real.png)

Your agent reproduces each bug with a failing probe, looks for who already solved the general problem, and fixes the system instead of patching one case. It commits small checked changes, safely, even when several agents share one folder.

Use it when:
- The same bug keeps coming back after "fixes".
- Your agent hand-codes something an engine or library already does.
- Several agent sessions commit to one checkout and keep undoing each other.

Try it: "The units keep walking through buildings. Fix the real problem, not this one case."

# Test your app one module at a time, the way a user sees it
![How click-everything works](../../../assets/skills/click-everything.png)

Your agent lists every route from your router, screenshots every page and state, presses the buttons, makes the app produce real output and reads it, fixes what doesn't make sense, and adds end-to-end tests so each fix stays fixed. You get a report per module with real counts.

## Use it when
- Your agent has nothing else queued.
- You want a module checked by eye, not just by passing tests.
- Pages look fine but the answers, reports or results inside them might not be.

Try it: "Use click-everything on the billing module."

# Tests that prove what your users actually do

![How test-like-a-user works](../../../assets/skills/test-like-a-user.png)

Your agent writes and reviews tests that walk the real user journey through the real app, with fakes only at the edges you can't control. You get tests that fail when the product breaks, not tests that pass because they mocked everything.

Use it when:
- Your agent is writing or fixing tests and you want them to mean something.
- You want an audit of an existing test suite.
- A redesign or migration needs proof that nothing got lost and nothing is duplicated.

Try it: "Review the tests in this PR against test-like-a-user and tell me which ones would pass with the feature deleted."

# Decision table template

One table per kind of model (chat, image, voice, ...). One row per model. Sort by call, then by gain.

| Call | Model | Replaces | Gain (benchmark, date read) | Cost | Effort | Platforms today → after | Licence (commercial use) | Risks | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Replace | `maker/new-model` (4B, Q4 build, 2.6 GB) | `maker/old-model` | 41 vs 33 on <benchmark>, read YYYY-MM-DD | 2.6 GB download; runs well on 8 GB phones and 8 GB desktops | M: needs a companion text encoder | desktop → desktop, Android, iOS | Apache-2.0 (yes) | Runtime support not yet confirmed on iOS | [model card](...), [leaderboard](...) |
| Keep | `maker/current-best` | | 52, read YYYY-MM-DD | | | | | | |
| Later | ... | | | | | | | | |
| Remove | ... | | | | | | | | |

Rules for filling it in:

- **Call** is one of Add, Replace, Keep, Later, Remove.
- **Gain** compares the same benchmark for both models, with the date it was read. "Not listed" when a model is
  not on the board. Never estimate a score.
- **Cost** is the download size and the smallest device that runs it well for on-device models, or the cost per
  call and latency for hosted ones.
- **Effort** is S (list entry only), M (small runtime or config work) or L (new runtime, new feature), plus what.
- Every fact in the row has a linked source.

Above the tables, put one line per device class with the Fast, Balanced and Best pick for each kind.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Rebuild the root README and each set's README from scripts/catalog.json.

    python3 scripts/build-readmes.py

Edit the catalog, not the READMEs. Skill READMEs (inside each skill folder) are written by hand.
"""
import json, os

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
cat = json.load(open(os.path.join(ROOT, "scripts", "catalog.json")))
sets = cat["sets"]
total = sum(len(s["skills"]) for s in sets)
plug = lambda s: s.get("plugin", s["dir"])


def table(s, prefix=""):
    rows = ["| Skill | What you get |", "| --- | --- |"]
    for name, line in s["skills"]:
        rows.append(f"| [**{name}**]({prefix}skills/{name}) | {line} |")
    return "\n".join(rows)


# Set pictures live in assets/sets, outside the plugin folders (each set folder is submitted to the Claude directory on its own).
img = lambda s, pre="../": (f"![How {s['title'].lower()} works]({pre}assets/sets/{s['dir']}-how-it-works.png)\n\n"
                            if os.path.exists(os.path.join(ROOT, "assets", "sets", s["dir"] + "-how-it-works.png")) else "")

for s in sets:
    body = f"""# {s['title']}

{s['pitch']}

{img(s)}{table(s)}

## Install just this set

```bash
npx skills add off-grid-ai/skills --skill {' '.join(n for n, _ in s['skills'])}
```

Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add off-grid-ai/skills` then `/plugin install {plug(s)}@off-grid-ai`.
Codex: `codex plugin marketplace add off-grid-ai/skills` then `codex plugin add {plug(s)}@off-grid-ai`.

Some of these skills call skills in other sets. To get everything working together, install every set (see the main README).

[All skills](../README.md)
"""
    open(os.path.join(ROOT, s["dir"], "README.md"), "w").write(body)


sections = "\n\n".join(
    f"### [{s['title']}]({s['dir']})\n\n{s['pitch']}\n\n{img(s, '')}{table(s, s['dir'] + '/')}" for s in sets)
hero = ("![How it works: you ask for a change, your agent maps everything it touches, makes it, checks it, and hands you one page with only the calls that need you](assets/how-it-works.png)\n\n"
        if os.path.exists(os.path.join(ROOT, "assets", "how-it-works.png")) else "")

where = {n: f"{s['dir']}/skills/{n}" for s in sets for n, _ in s["skills"]}
hooks = "\n".join(f"- [{s['title']}]({s['dir']})" for s in sets)

readme = f"""# Stop babysitting your AI. Make it build, test and ship like a senior team.

[![graph-engineering on a real change: every screen the AI changed, before and after on one page. 105 screens from one ask across 7 apps, and only the calls that need you](assets/graph-engineering-demo.gif)](assets/graph-engineering-demo.mp4)

These are the skills I use every day. I built [Off Grid AI](https://github.com/off-grid-ai/OGAM) on my own with them, and it reached 250,000+ downloads on 7 platforms without spending a dollar on ads. Install them and your AI works the way mine does.

[![Off Grid AI, built by one person with these skills: 250,000+ organic downloads on 7 platforms](assets/built-with-these-skills.png)](https://github.com/alichherawalla)

## What these skills do

Vibe coding gets you a demo in an afternoon. Then your AI breaks things that already worked, every screen looks like every other AI app, and you're asked to approve 50 changed files you can't read.

Each skill is a short playbook your agent reads before it starts, so it tests every change in your real app and checks the design before you see anything. What you get back is one page with every screen before and after, and only the decisions that need you. They're free, MIT licensed, and work in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and 60+ other agents.

{hooks}

{hero}## Install in one line

Paste this into your agent:

```text

```

**[resume-any-chat](%(rac)s): never lose a chat again.** Find any past session by its name, even from another account or from Codex, and carry on where it stopped.

## Good to know

- Each skill is a folder with a `SKILL.md`, plain Markdown your agent reads when your request matches it. Nothing runs until you ask.
- Review pages publish as Claude Artifacts when you have them, and as a local HTML page when you don't.
- Skills mention each other by name. Install the whole set to get everything working together.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install every skill for every agent on this machine, with no Node needed.
#
#   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/off-grid-ai/skills/main/install.sh | bash
#   bash install.sh             install or update
#   bash install.sh --uninstall remove the links this script made
#
# It keeps one copy in ~/.off-grid-skills (git pull to update) and links each skill into the skills folder of
# every agent it finds: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, OpenCode, Kiro, and any
# agent that reads ~/.agents/skills.
set -euo pipefail

REPO="${OFF_GRID_SKILLS_REPO:-https://github.com/off-grid-ai/skills.git}"
HOME_DIR="${OFF_GRID_SKILLS_HOME:-$HOME/.off-grid-skills}"

# agent config folder (detect) -> its global skills folder
TARGETS=(
  "$HOME/.claude|$HOME/.claude/skills"
  "$HOME/.agents|$HOME/.agents/skills"
  "$HOME/.codex|$HOME/.agents/skills"
  "$HOME/.cursor|$HOME/.cursor/skills"
  "$HOME/.gemini|$HOME/.gemini/skills"
  "$HOME/.copilot|$HOME/.copilot/skills"
  "$HOME/.codeium/windsurf|$HOME/.codeium/windsurf/skills"
  "$HOME/.config/opencode|$HOME/.config/opencode/skills"
  "$HOME/.kiro|$HOME/.kiro/skills"
)

skills() { find "$HOME_DIR" -mindepth 4 -maxdepth 4 -path "*/skills/*" -name SKILL.md -not -path '*/.git/*' -exec dirname {} \; | sort; }

if [[ "${1:-}" == "--uninstall" ]]; then
  for t in "${TARGETS[@]}"; do
    dest="${t#*|}"; [[ -d "$dest" ]] || continue
    for link in "$dest"/*; do
      [[ -L "$link" && "$(readlink "$link")" == "$HOME_DIR"/* ]] && rm "$link" && echo "removed $link"
    done
  done
  exit 0
fi

command -v git >/dev/null || { echo "git is required"; exit 1; }
if [[ -d "$HOME_DIR/.git" ]]; then
  git -C "$HOME_DIR" pull --ff-only --quiet
else
  git clone --depth 1 --quiet "$REPO" "$HOME_DIR"
fi

linked=0; agents=()
for t in "${TARGETS[@]}"; do
  detect="${t%%|*}"; dest="${t#*|}"
  # always install for the shared ~/.agents/skills folder; others only if that agent is installed
  [[ -d "$detect" || "$dest" == "$HOME/.agents/skills" ]] || continue
  [[ " ${agents[*]-} " == *" $dest "* ]] && continue
  agents+=("$dest"); mkdir -p "$dest"
  while read -r s; do
    name="$(basename "$s")"; link="$dest/$name"
    if [[ -e "$link" && ! -L "$link" ]]; then echo "skipped $link (you already have a skill with this name)"; continue; fi
    ln -sfn "$s" "$link"; linked=$((linked + 1))
  done < <(skills)
done

echo "Installed $(skills | wc -l | tr -d ' ') skills into ${#agents[@]} agent folders:"
printf '  %s\n' "${agents[@]}"
echo "Update any time: bash $HOME_DIR/install.sh"
echo "Try it in your agent: \"Use graph-engineering to rename one thing across the app.\""
